scope.evidence: Every hunk serves the ticket: prefix resolution and map handling (app/Models/Queue.php:18-51), daily sequencing (app/Models/Ticket.php:37-54), issuance (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:43-54), map updates (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:20,57-66), factory support (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:34,55) and schema changes (database/migrations/...add_issue_date...). No unrelated refactors, files or features.

issues.explanation: `priority_prefix_map` is added to `#[Fillable]`, so any user-controlled array reaching a Queue fill/create call can set the map, directly violating the task's 'The map is not mass-assignable from user input'.

Requirement 2 asks that validation be enforced whenever a queue is saved and throw `InvalidArgumentException` from the model, and that an empty map be normalized to null on every save; neither exists, so `Queue::factory()->create(['priority_prefix_map' => ['0' => 'xx']])` or any direct save persists an invalid map.

issue_date defaults to today instead of the date of issued_at, so `Ticket::factory()->create(['issued_at' => '2026-09-28'])` is not aligned and allocates the wrong day's code; line 55 also passes a Carbon `$ticket->issue_date` into a `string` parameter, which serialises as 'Y-m-d H:i:s' and no longer matches the stored 'Y-m-d' value on SQLite, making repeated same-day allocations return 001 and collide on the unique index.

The clock is read twice (`$issueDate = now()` then `'issued_at' => now()`), so a request at midnight can store a code for one day and an issued_at on the next, exactly the split requirement 4 forbids.

The 'make it non-nullable' step uses `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL` (PostgreSQL-only) inside a catch-all that swallows the exception, and the comment says SQLite is skipped, so issue_date remains nullable on the project's actual database and the migration requirement is unmet.
Requirement 7 asks for `docs/business-rules.md` ('Display code'), `docs/database-schema.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` updates, and none are in the diff.
No Pest/PHPUnit test covers the prefix mapping, daily reset, validation, migration backfill or factory behaviour, contrary to the project's mandatory test-first rule.
The new column is added to an already-shipped create migration instead of a new `make:migration` file, so existing deployments that already ran it will never receive `queues.priority_prefix_map`.

`ValidationException::withMessages` is introduced without any added `use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;` hunk, which in the `App\Actions` namespace resolves to a non-existent class and is fatal unless the file already imported it (not verifiable from the diff).

When the map is valid the queue has already been mutated earlier in the method, and when validation throws the in-memory model is left with the rejected map and any other pending changes, so only the database (not the object handed back to the caller) is 'unchanged'.
Each allocation re-fetches the queue with `findOrFail` although `IssueTicket` already holds the locked queue, adding a redundant query inside the locked transaction.

The default map is duplicated as a literal in the action and as an unused `DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP` constant in the model, so the two can drift; the constant is dead code because prefixForPriority hard-codes the ranges.
The new `$code = ...` line is indented four levels shallower than its neighbours, which Pint's `--test` would flag.
`use App\Models\Queue;` is redundant inside the same namespace and `use App\Models\Ticket;` in the migration is unused.

review.summary: The change adds priority prefixes, a per-queue map on Queue/UpdateQueue, daily issue_date sequencing in Ticket::nextCode, and the supporting column/index, but several core guarantees are broken. issue_date is never actually made NOT NULL, the factory ignores issued_at and passes a Carbon where a date string is expected, IssueTicket reads the clock twice, model-level validation/normalization and the docs are missing, the map is mass-assignable, and no tests exist; that is substantial rework before this can merge.
